subject: bedroom light at night
title: What If You Always Slept With the Light On?

scenes.text: What if you always slept with the light on? You'd sleep, but your heart wouldn't rest.
Northwestern scientists had healthy young adults sleep one night in dim light, and one under ordinary room lighting.
Under the light, their heart rate stayed higher all night, even though they were asleep.
The next morning, their bodies handled sugar worse. Insulin resistance went up after just one night.
In a separate study of older adults, those exposed to light at night were more likely to have obesity, diabetes and high blood pressure.
Your eyes are shut. Your body still knows the lights are on.

description:
What if you always slept with the light on? In a 2022 PNAS study from Northwestern Medicine, one night of sleep under overhead room lighting raised heart rate during sleep and increased insulin resistance the next morning, compared with a dim room.
A separate 2022 study of older adults linked light exposure at night with higher rates of obesity, diabetes and high blood pressure (an association, not proof of cause).
